```{r}
#| label: load-packages-r

library(tidyverse)
library(tidyfinance)
library(nanoparquet)
library(slider)
library(tsgarch)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)

# Daily variances times 252 are annual variances
days_per_year <- 252

# The SPY data of lecture 16: March of every year
years <- 2008:2025
sample_month <- 3
recent_year <- 2024
crash_day <- ymd("2020-03-12")

# Continuous trading as in lecture 16, without the snapshots of the opening
# auction (9:30:05) and the closing auction (16:00:00)
first_snapshot <- hms::parse_hms("09:30:10")
last_snapshot <- hms::parse_hms("15:59:55")
snapshot_seconds <- 5
trading_day_seconds <- 6.5 * 3600

# The forecasts: estimated until the end of 2020, evaluated from 2021 on. The
# code on the slides defines these constants again
estimation_end <- ymd("2020-12-31")
days_week <- 5
days_month <- 22

# Colours of the slides, used by the figures
ku_red <- "#901A1E"
jet <- "#3d3d3d"
grey <- "#666666"
light <- "#e6e3df"
theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
)

# Daily variances (decimals) as annualized volatilities, and dates for the text
annualized <- \(variance) sqrt(days_per_year * variance)
day_label <- \(day) paste(mday(day), month.name[month(day)], year(day))
month_label <- \(year) paste(month.name[sample_month], year)

source("lecture-slides/_live-poll.R")
forecast_poll <- "aef27-l17-forecast-volatility"
```

```{r}
#| label: volatility-forecasts
#| include: false
#| cache: true
# VOLARE: the E-mini S&P 500 futures (ES) and the 30 Dow Jones stocks. Daily
# close-to-close returns in percent and realized variances (5-minute returns)
# in squared percent. VOLARE's prices are not adjusted for splits: an
# overnight fall below 60% of the price is a split (8 in the Dow Jones stocks,
# 2:1 to 20:1), with the rounded price ratio as the split ratio
split_threshold <- log(0.6)
volare <- bind_rows(
  read_parquet("data/volare_futures_realized_measures_daily.parquet") |>
    filter(symbol == "ES"),
  read_parquet("data/volare_stocks_realized_measures_daily.parquet") |>
    filter(dow30)
) |>
  select(symbol, date, open_price, close_price, rv5) |>
  arrange(symbol, date) |>
  mutate(
    overnight = log(open_price / lag(close_price)),
    split_ratio = if_else(
      overnight < split_threshold,
      round(exp(-overnight)),
      1,
      missing = 1
    ),
    ret = 100 * (overnight + log(split_ratio) + log(close_price / open_price)),
    rv = 1e4 * rv5,
    rv_week = slide_dbl(rv, mean, .before = days_week - 1, .complete = TRUE),
    rv_month = slide_dbl(rv, mean, .before = days_month - 1, .complete = TRUE),
    rv_next = lead(rv),
    ret_next = lead(ret),
    .by = symbol
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(overnight))

# GARCH(1,1) with a constant mean, by maximum likelihood until the end of
# 2020; then the forecast of the next day's variance at every day
garch_forecast <- function(data) {
  estimation <- data |> filter(date <= estimation_end)
  fit <- garch_modelspec(
    xts::xts(estimation$ret, estimation$date),
    model = "garch",
    order = c(1, 1),
    constant = TRUE
  ) |>
    estimate()
  p <- coef(fit)
  shock <- data$ret - p[["mu"]]
  variance <- numeric(length(shock))
  variance[1] <- var(shock[data$date <= estimation_end])
  for (t in seq_along(shock)[-1]) {
    variance[t] <- p[["omega"]] +
      p[["alpha1"]] * shock[t - 1]^2 +
      p[["beta1"]] * variance[t - 1]
  }
  list(
    parameters = p,
    forecast = p[["omega"]] + p[["alpha1"]] * shock^2 + p[["beta1"]] * variance
  )
}

# Five forecasts of the next day's realized variance. GARCH forecasts the
# close-to-close variance, but RV covers only the trading hours of the stocks:
# the GARCH forecast is scaled by the estimation sample's ratio of mean RV to
# mean forecast
forecast_models <- c(
  "Today's RV",
  "Last 22 days",
  "GARCH(1,1)",
  "HAR",
  "log-HAR"
)
forecast_symbol <- function(data) {
  estimation <- data |>
    filter(date <= estimation_end) |>
    drop_na(rv_month, rv_next)
  har <- lm(rv_next ~ rv + rv_week + rv_month, data = estimation)
  log_har <- lm(
    log(rv_next) ~ log(rv) + log(rv_week) + log(rv_month),
    data = estimation
  )
  garch <- garch_forecast(data)
  in_estimation <- data$date %in% estimation$date
  garch_scale <- mean(data$rv_next[in_estimation]) /
    mean(garch$forecast[in_estimation])
  forecasts <- data |>
    mutate(
      garch_unscaled = garch$forecast,
      "Today's RV" = rv,
      "Last 22 days" = rv_month,
      "GARCH(1,1)" = garch_scale * garch_unscaled,
      HAR = predict(har, newdata = data),
      "log-HAR" = exp(predict(log_har, newdata = data) + sigma(log_har)^2 / 2)
    )
  tibble(
    forecasts = list(forecasts),
    alpha = garch$parameters[["alpha1"]],
    beta = garch$parameters[["beta1"]],
    omega = garch$parameters[["omega"]],
    garch_scale = garch_scale
  )
}
volatility_forecasts <- volare |>
  nest(data = -symbol) |>
  mutate(result = map(data, forecast_symbol)) |>
  select(symbol, result) |>
  unnest(result)

# Out of sample: every day from 2021 on with a next-day RV
test_forecasts <- volatility_forecasts |>
  select(symbol, forecasts) |>
  unnest(forecasts) |>
  filter(date > estimation_end, !is.na(rv_next))
forecast_losses <- test_forecasts |>
  pivot_longer(
    all_of(forecast_models),
    names_to = "model",
    values_to = "forecast"
  ) |>
  summarize(
    mse = mean((rv_next - forecast)^2),
    qlike = mean(rv_next / forecast - log(rv_next / forecast) - 1),
    mz_r2 = cor(rv_next, forecast)^2,
    lowest_forecast = min(forecast),
    .by = c(symbol, model)
  )
stopifnot(all(forecast_losses$lowest_forecast > 0))
```

```{r}
#| label: garch-numbers
#| include: false
es_garch <- volatility_forecasts |> filter(symbol == "ES")
es_persistence <- es_garch$alpha + es_garch$beta
es_half_life <- log(0.5) / log(es_persistence)
es_long_run_volatility <- sqrt(
  days_per_year * es_garch$omega / (1 - es_persistence)
) /
  100
stocks_garch <- volatility_forecasts |>
  filter(symbol != "ES") |>
  summarize(
    alpha = median(alpha),
    beta = median(beta),
    garch_scale = median(garch_scale)
  )
es_start <- min(volare$date[volare$symbol == "ES"])
```

## From the bid-ask bounce to volatility

- **Lecture 16:** trade prices bounce between the bid and the ask, so their changes are negatively autocorrelated, $\text{Cov}(\Delta p_t, \Delta p_{t-1}) = -s^2/4$. The more often we sample, the more of this noise we measure
- **Lectures 2 to 5:** portfolio choice needs the covariance matrix, estimated from monthly returns (60 months in lecture 3). Volatility changes much faster than that
- **Assignment 3 (6 to 13 May):** realized volatility from the SPY snapshots of lecture 16 and from VOLARE, and forecasts of it

::: {.highlight}
**Today:** measure a day's volatility from intraday returns, keep microstructure noise out of the measure, and forecast tomorrow's volatility with GARCH and HAR
:::

```{r}
  mutate(volatility = annualized(rv5))
episodes <- tibble(

)
peaks <- es_daily |>
  mutate(month = floor_date(date, "month")) |>
  inner_join(episodes, by = "month") |>
  slice_max(volatility, n = 1, by = month)
calmest_year <- es_daily |>
  mutate(year = year(date)) |>

  summarize(volatility = median(volatility), .by = year) |>

ggplot(es_daily, aes(x = date, y = volatility)) +
```

- The E-mini S&P 500 futures (ES) in VOLARE (Cipollini et al., 2026): every trading day's realized volatility from five-minute returns, annualized, `r month.name[month(es_start)]` `r year(es_start)` to `r month.name[month(max(es_daily$date))]` `r year(max(es_daily$date))`
- The median day has `r percent(median(es_daily$volatility), 0.1)`, the median day of `r calmest_year$year` only `r percent(calmest_year$volatility, 0.1)`. Calm and turbulent days come in clusters: the most volatile days all fall in a few weeks

## GARCH(1,1)

::: {.box}
Engle (1982) and Bollerslev (1986): the daily return is $r_{t+1} = \mu + \varepsilon_{t+1}$, and the variance of tomorrow's shock depends on today's shock and today's variance
:::

$$
\sigma^2_{t+1} = \omega + \alpha\, \varepsilon_t^2 + \beta\, \sigma^2_t \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad E_t\big[\sigma^2_{t+h}\big] - \bar\sigma^2 = (\alpha + \beta)^{h-1} \big(\sigma^2_{t+1} - \bar\sigma^2\big)
$$

- **Persistence** $\alpha + \beta < 1$: forecasts return to the long-run variance $\bar\sigma^2 = \omega / (1 - \alpha - \beta)$, and a shock to the variance halves after $\ln 0.5 / \ln(\alpha + \beta)$ days
- Estimated by maximum likelihood with normal shocks, on the close-to-close returns of ES until `r year(estimation_end)`: $\alpha =$ `r number(es_garch$alpha, 0.01)`, $\beta =$ `r number(es_garch$beta, 0.01)`, a persistence of `r number(es_persistence, 0.01)`, a half-life of `r round(es_half_life)` days and a long-run volatility of `r percent(es_long_run_volatility, 0.1)` a year. The 30 Dow Jones stocks (median): $\alpha =$ `r number(stocks_garch$alpha, 0.01)`, $\beta =$ `r number(stocks_garch$beta, 0.01)`
- GARCH needs only daily returns: the benchmark for the forecasts from intraday data. R: `tsgarch`, Python: `arch`

# Realized variance

## Quadratic variation

::: {.box}
Within a day, the log price moves as $dp_t = \mu_t\, dt + \sigma_t\, dW_t$, and its variance $\sigma_t^2$ changes during the day. The day's variance is the **integrated variance** $IV = \int_0^1 \sigma_t^2\, dt$. Can we measure it from $n$ intraday returns $r_i = p_{i/n} - p_{(i-1)/n}$?
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$
RV_n = \sum_{i=1}^{n} r_i^2 \;\longrightarrow\; IV \quad (n \to \infty), \qquad RV_n - IV \approx N\Big(0, \frac{2\, IQ}{n}\Big), \qquad IQ = \int_0^1 \sigma_t^4\, dt
$$

- **Realized variance** measures the day's variance without a model: the sum of squared returns converges to the quadratic variation of the price (Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard, 2002; Andersen, Bollerslev, Diebold & Labys, 2003)
- The drift does not matter: its share in $RV_n$ vanishes as $n$ grows. Jumps do: with jumps, $RV_n$ converges to $IV$ plus the squared jumps
- More returns make the measure more precise. The **realized quarticity** $RQ_n = \frac{n}{3} \sum_{i} r_i^4$ estimates the integrated quarticity $IQ$
:::

## Realized variance in code

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```{r}
#| label: realized-variance-r
# Continuous trading as in lecture 16: without the snapshots of the opening
# auction (9:30:05) and the closing auction (16:00:00)
first_snapshot <- hms::parse_hms("09:30:10")
last_snapshot <- hms::parse_hms("15:59:55")
sampling_interval <- "5 minutes"

# Each day: the last midquote of every interval, the log returns between
# them, and the sum of their squares
spy_rv <- spy |>
  filter(between(hms::as_hms(ts), first_snapshot, last_snapshot)) |>
  mutate(day = as_date(ts), interval = floor_date(ts, sampling_interval)) |>
  summarize(log_price = log(last(midquote)), .by = c(day, interval)) |>
  mutate(ret = log_price - lag(log_price), .by = day) |>
  summarize(
    rv = sum(ret^2, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_returns = sum(!is.na(ret)),
    .by = day
  )
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: realized-variance-py
#| eval: false
# Continuous trading as in lecture 16: without the snapshots of the opening
# auction (9:30:05) and the closing auction (16:00:00)
first_snapshot = time(9, 30, 10)
last_snapshot = time(15, 59, 55)
sampling_interval = "5m"

# Each day: the last midquote of every interval, the log returns between
# them, and the sum of their squares
spy_rv = (
    spy.filter(pl.col("ts").dt.time().is_between(first_snapshot, last_snapshot))
    .with_columns(
        day=pl.col("ts").dt.date(),
        interval=pl.col("ts").dt.truncate(sampling_interval),
    )
    .group_by("day", "interval", maintain_order=True)
    .agg(log_price=pl.col("midquote").last().log())
    .with_columns(ret=pl.col("log_price").diff().over("day"))
    .group_by("day", maintain_order=True)
    .agg(rv=(pl.col("ret") ** 2).sum(), n_returns=pl.col("ret").count())
)
```
:::

```{r}
#| label: realized-variance-numbers
#| include: false
# The median day of the recent March: of an even number of days, the lower
# of the two middle ones
recent_rv <- spy_rv |> filter(year(day) == recent_year)
calm_day <- recent_rv |>
  filter(rv == quantile(rv, 0.5, type = 1)) |>
  pull(day)
snapshots_per_day <- (as.numeric(last_snapshot - first_snapshot)) /
  snapshot_seconds +
  1
```

## Realized variance builds up during the day

```{r}
#| label: plot-build-up
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3.3
# The five-minute returns of two days, as in the code: squared returns in
# squared percent and their running sum, at the end of each interval
build_up <- spy |>
  filter(
    between(hms::as_hms(ts), first_snapshot, last_snapshot),
    as_date(ts) %in% c(calm_day, crash_day)
  ) |>
  mutate(day = as_date(ts), interval = floor_date(ts, "5 minutes")) |>
  summarize(log_price = log(last(midquote)), .by = c(day, interval)) |>
  mutate(ret = log_price - lag(log_price), .by = day) |>
  drop_na() |>
  mutate(
    squared = 1e4 * ret^2,
    running_sum = cumsum(squared),
    clock = hour(interval) + minute(interval) / 60 + 5 / 60,
    .by = day
  ) |>
  left_join(spy_rv, by = "day") |>
  mutate(
    panel = paste0(
      day_label(day),
      ": annualized volatility ",
      percent(annualized(rv), 0.1)
    ),
    panel = fct_reorder(panel, as.numeric(day))
  )
# The share of the five largest squared returns in the day's variance
n_largest <- 5
day_summary <- build_up |>
  summarize(
    rv = sum(squared),
    share = sum(sort(squared, decreasing = TRUE)[1:n_largest]) / sum(squared),
    .by = day
  )
calm_summary <- day_summary |> filter(day == calm_day)
crash_summary <- day_summary |> filter(day == crash_day)

ggplot(build_up, aes(x = clock)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = squared), fill = "#b3b3b3", width = 4 / 60) +
  geom_step(aes(y = running_sum), color = ku_red, linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(10, 12, 14, 16),
    labels = c("10:00", "12:00", "14:00", "16:00")
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Squared returns and their sum (%²)") +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 13, hjust = 0))
```

- `spy_rv` has `r comma(nrow(spy_rv))` days with `r unique(spy_rv$n_returns)` five-minute returns each (every snapshot: `r comma(snapshots_per_day - 1)`). Grey: the squared returns of two days, in %²; red: their running sum, which ends at the day's RV. Annualized: $\sqrt{252 \cdot RV}$
- `r day_label(crash_day)`: `r number(crash_summary$rv, 0.1)` %², `r round(crash_summary$rv / calm_summary$rv)` times as much as on `r day_label(calm_day)`, the median day of `r month_label(recent_year)` (`r number(calm_summary$rv, 0.01)` %²). On both days, the `r n_largest` largest returns carry about half of the variance (`r percent(crash_summary$share)` and `r percent(calm_summary$share)`)

## A better yardstick than squared returns

```{r}
#| label: plot-standardized-returns
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3.3
# ES: daily returns divided by their standard deviation, and by the day's
# realized volatility
kurtosis <- \(x) mean((x - mean(x))^4) / mean((x - mean(x))^2)^2
standardized <- es_daily |>
  transmute(
    by_sd = ret / sd(ret),
    by_rv = ret / sqrt(rv)
  )
es_kurtosis <- map_dbl(standardized, kurtosis)
histogram_panel <- function(column, label) {
  ggplot(standardized, aes(x = .data[[column]])) +
    geom_histogram(
      aes(y = after_stat(density)),
      binwidth = 0.25,
      fill = "#b3b3b3",
      color = "white"
    ) +
    stat_function(fun = dnorm, color = ku_red, linewidth = 0.9) +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = -5,
      y = 0.7,
      hjust = 0,
      label = paste("Kurtosis", number(es_kurtosis[[column]], 0.1)),
      color = jet
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-5, 5), ylim = c(0, 0.8)) +
    labs(x = label, y = "Density")
}
histogram_panel("by_sd", "Daily return / its standard deviation") +
  histogram_panel("by_rv", "Daily return / the day's realized volatility")

# The GARCH forecasts of ES out of sample against the next day's squared
# return and the next day's RV: R² of the regressions
es_test <- test_forecasts |> filter(symbol == "ES", !is.na(ret_next))
garch_r2 <- c(
  squared_return = cor(es_test$ret_next^2, es_test$garch_unscaled)^2,
  rv = cor(es_test$rv_next, es_test$garch_unscaled)^2
)
```

- ES's daily close-to-close returns have fat tails, a kurtosis of `r number(es_kurtosis[["by_sd"]], 0.1)`. Divided by the day's realized volatility, they are close to normal (red), with a kurtosis of `r number(es_kurtosis[["by_rv"]], 0.1)` (Andersen, Bollerslev, Diebold & Ebens, 2001, for stocks)
- So $r_t^2 \approx RV_t \cdot z_t^2$ with $z_t \sim N(0, 1)$: a squared return is the day's variance times noise. From 2021 on, the GARCH forecasts explain `r percent(garch_r2[["squared_return"]])` of the next day's $r^2$ ($R^2$ of a regression), but `r percent(garch_r2[["rv"]])` of the next day's RV (Andersen & Bollerslev, 1998)

# Microstructure noise

## What noise does to realized variance

::: {.box}
We observe $y_i = p_i + u_i$: the efficient log price plus noise $u_i$ from the bid-ask bounce and the tick size, independent over time, with variance $\omega^2$. What happens to realized variance?
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$
r^y_i = r_i + u_i - u_{i-1} \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad E\big[RV^y_n\big] = IV + 2n\,\omega^2, \qquad \text{Cov}\big(r^y_i, r^y_{i-1}\big) = -\omega^2
$$

- The bias grows with $n$: at the highest frequencies, realized variance measures mostly noise. Roll's model of lecture 16 is the case $\omega^2 = s^2/4$
- Precision against bias: the variance $2\, IQ/n$ falls with $n$, the squared bias $4n^2\omega^4$ rises. Their sum is smallest at $n^* \approx (IQ / 4\omega^4)^{1/3}$ (Bandi & Russell, 2008)
- In practice, five-minute returns are hard to beat for liquid stocks (Liu, Patton & Sheppard, 2015)
:::

```{r}
#| label: signature
#| include: false
# Trade prices from the snapshots: at the ask when buyers initiated more
# shares in the five seconds before the snapshot, at the bid when sellers
# did, and the last trade price when nobody traded
spy_continuous <- spy |>
  filter(between(hms::as_hms(ts), first_snapshot, last_snapshot)) |>
  mutate(
    day = as_date(ts),
    midquote_log = log(midquote),
    trade_log = if_else(
      signed_volume != 0,
      midquote_log + sign(signed_volume) * spread / 2 / 1e4,
      NA_real_
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(day) |>
  fill(trade_log, .direction = "downup") |>
  ungroup()

# Realized variance with one price per interval of `seconds`: the last
# snapshot of each interval, as in the code
rv_by_interval <- function(seconds, price) {
  interval <- as.numeric(spy_continuous$ts) %/% seconds
  last_in_interval <- interval != lead(interval, default = Inf)
  spy_continuous[last_in_interval, ] |>
    summarize(rv = sum(diff(.data[[price]])^2), .by = c(year, day))
}
intervals <- c(5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 120, 300, 600, 900, 1800)
prices <- c("Midquotes" = "midquote_log", "Trade prices" = "trade_log")
signature <- expand_grid(seconds = intervals, price = names(prices)) |>
  mutate(rv = map2(seconds, price, \(s, p) rv_by_interval(s, prices[[p]]))) |>
  unnest(rv)
stopifnot(all.equal(
  signature |>
    filter(seconds == 300, price == "Midquotes") |>
    pull(rv),
  spy_rv$rv
))
signature_years <- signature |>
  summarize(volatility = annualized(mean(rv)), .by = c(price, seconds, year))

# 5-second against 5-minute RV in every March; the March with the most noise
# in trade prices
noise_by_year <- signature |>
  filter(seconds %in% c(snapshot_seconds, 300)) |>
  summarize(rv = mean(rv), .by = c(price, seconds, year)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = seconds, values_from = rv, names_prefix = "rv_") |>
  mutate(ratio = rv_5 / rv_300)
noisiest_year <- noise_by_year |>
  filter(price == "Trade prices") |>
  slice_max(ratio, n = 1) |>
  pull(year)

# Five-second trade price returns: their autocorrelation in every March, and
# Roll's half spread from their autocovariance (bps)
trade_returns <- spy_continuous |>
  mutate(
    trade_return = trade_log - lag(trade_log),
    previous = lag(trade_return),
    .by = day
  ) |>
  drop_na(trade_return, previous)
bounce_by_year <- trade_returns |>
  summarize(
    autocorrelation = cor(trade_return, previous),
    roll_half_spread = 1e4 * sqrt(-cov(trade_return, previous)),
    median_half_spread = median(spread) / 2,
    .by = year
  )
bounce_noisiest <- bounce_by_year |> filter(year == noisiest_year)
bounce_split <- 2018
bounce_ranges <- bounce_by_year |>
  mutate(period = year <= bounce_split) |>
  summarize(
    lowest = min(autocorrelation),
    highest = max(autocorrelation),
    .by = period
  )

# Bandi & Russell: the optimal number of returns from the realized quarticity
# of 5-minute midquote returns and the noise variance of trade prices
day_quarticity <- spy_continuous |>
  filter(year == noisiest_year) |>
  mutate(interval = floor_date(ts, "5 minutes")) |>
  summarize(log_price = last(midquote_log), .by = c(day, interval)) |>
  mutate(ret = log_price - lag(log_price), .by = day) |>
  summarize(rq = sum(!is.na(ret)) / 3 * sum(ret^4, na.rm = TRUE), .by = day)
optimal_sampling <- trade_returns |>
  filter(year == noisiest_year) |>
  summarize(noise_variance = -cov(trade_return, previous), .by = day) |>
  left_join(day_quarticity, by = "day") |>
  mutate(
    n_optimal = (rq / (4 * noise_variance^2))^(1 / 3),
    seconds = trading_day_seconds / n_optimal
  )
optimal_seconds <- median(optimal_sampling$seconds)

# Two-scale realized variance (Zhang, Mykland & Aït-Sahalia, 2005): the average
# of K sparse grids minus the bias, estimated from all returns
tsrv <- function(log_price, K) {
  n <- length(log_price) - 1
  rv_all <- sum(diff(log_price)^2)
  rv_sparse <- map_dbl(seq_len(K), \(k) {
    sum(diff(log_price[seq(k, length(log_price), by = K)])^2)
  })
  n_bar <- (n - K + 1) / K
  (mean(rv_sparse) - n_bar / n * rv_all) / (1 - n_bar / n)
}
tsrv_grids <- 300 / snapshot_seconds
spy_tsrv <- spy_continuous |>
  summarize(
    Midquotes = tsrv(midquote_log, tsrv_grids),
    "Trade prices" = tsrv(trade_log, tsrv_grids),
    .by = c(year, day)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Midquotes, "Trade prices"), names_to = "price") |>
  summarize(tsrv = annualized(mean(value)), .by = c(price, year))
tsrv_table <- signature_years |>
  filter(year == noisiest_year, seconds %in% c(snapshot_seconds, 300)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = seconds, values_from = volatility) |>
  left_join(spy_tsrv, by = c("price", "year"))
tsrv_against_midquotes <- spy_tsrv |>
  filter(price == "Trade prices") |>
  left_join(
    signature_years |> filter(price == "Midquotes", seconds == 300),
    by = "year"
  ) |>
  mutate(ratio = tsrv / volatility)
```

- The bounce shrank with the spread: the autocorrelation of five-second trade price returns lay between `r number(bounce_ranges$lowest[bounce_ranges$period], 0.01, style_negative = "minus")` and `r number(bounce_ranges$highest[bounce_ranges$period], 0.01, style_negative = "minus")` until `r bounce_split`, and between `r number(bounce_ranges$lowest[!bounce_ranges$period], 0.01, style_negative = "minus")` and `r number(bounce_ranges$highest[!bounce_ranges$period], 0.01, style_negative = "minus")` since. Midquotes barely bounce

## Two-scale realized variance

::: {.box}
Zhang, Mykland & Aït-Sahalia (2005): use every price, but remove the noise. Returns over $K$ snapshots carry little noise, returns between neighbouring snapshots mostly noise. Combine both
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$
TSRV = \Big(1 - \frac{\bar n}{n}\Big)^{-1} \Big( \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k=1}^{K} RV^{(k)} - \frac{\bar n}{n}\, RV^{\text{all}} \Big), \qquad \bar n = \frac{n - K + 1}{K}
$$

- $RV^{(k)}$ uses every $K$-th price from price $k$ on; the average over $k = 1, \dots, K$ uses all data and has the bias $2\bar n\, \omega^2$. $RV^{\text{all}} / 2n$ estimates $\omega^2$, so the second term removes the bias
- SPY, `r month_label(noisiest_year)`, $K =$ `r tsrv_grids`: five minutes on the five-second grid. In every March, TSRV on trade prices lies within `r percent(max(abs(tsrv_against_midquotes$ratio - 1)))` of five-minute RV on midquotes

```{r}
#| label: tsrv-table
#| echo: false
tsrv_table |>
  transmute(
    Price = price,
    "Every 5 seconds" = percent(`5`, 0.1),
    "Every 5 minutes" = percent(`300`, 0.1),
    TSRV = percent(tsrv, 0.1)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrr")
```
:::

## Realized kernels

::: {.box}
Noise makes neighbouring returns negatively correlated. Instead of sampling less often, add the autocovariances of the returns to the realized variance
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$
RK = \sum_{h=-H}^{H} k\Big(\frac{h}{H+1}\Big)\, \gamma_h, \qquad \gamma_h = \sum_{i} r_i\, r_{i-|h|}
$$

- $\gamma_0$ is the realized variance. With independent noise, $\gamma_{1}$ and $\gamma_{-1}$ are about $-n\omega^2$ each: added with full weight, they cancel the bias $2n\omega^2$
- The weights $k(\cdot)$ fall smoothly from 1 to 0 over $H$ lags, which grows with the noise: the estimator is consistent, and with the Parzen weights never negative (Barndorff-Nielsen, Hansen, Lunde & Shephard, 2008, 2011)
- No noise model beyond the autocovariances and no sparse grid: VOLARE reports a realized kernel for every day
:::

```{r}
#| label: volare-measures

# The measures of the 30 Dow Jones stocks relative to rv5: ratios of means
dow_measures <- read_parquet(
  "data/volare_stocks_realized_measures_daily.parquet"
) |>
  filter(dow30)
relative_to_rv5 <- map_dbl(
  set_names(c("rv1", "rk", "bv5", "rsp5", "rsn5")),
  \(measure) mean(dow_measures[[measure]]) / mean(dow_measures$rv5)
)
noise_by_stock <- dow_measures |>
  summarize(
    ratio = mean(rv1) / mean(rv5),
    trades = median(trades),
    .by = symbol
  )
noise_trades_correlation <- cor(
  noise_by_stock$ratio,
  log(noise_by_stock$trades)
)
n_dow_days <- n_distinct(dow_measures$date)
dow_start <- min(dow_measures$date)
rm(dow_measures)
```

## Realized measures in VOLARE

- VOLARE (Cipollini et al., 2026) on Absalon: realized measures of 40 US stocks (the 30 Dow Jones stocks have `dow30`) on `r comma(n_dow_days)` days from `r day_label(dow_start)`, and of five futures, ES among them, from `r month.name[month(es_start)]` `r year(es_start)`, all until October 2026
- One row per asset and day. Variances are daily, in squared decimal returns: $\sqrt{252 \cdot \text{rv5}}$ is the annualized volatility, $10^4 \cdot \text{rv5}$ the variance in squared percent

| Column | Measure | Dow Jones stocks, mean relative to rv5 |
|:--|:--|--:|
| `rv5`, `rv1` | Realized variance from 5- and 1-minute returns | 1 and `r number(relative_to_rv5[["rv1"]], 0.01)` |
| `rk` | Realized kernel | `r number(relative_to_rv5[["rk"]], 0.01)` |
| `bv5` | Bipower variation $\frac{\pi}{2} \sum_i \lvert r_i \rvert \lvert r_{i-1} \rvert$: robust to jumps | `r number(relative_to_rv5[["bv5"]], 0.01)` |
| `rsp5`, `rsn5` | Semivariances: $\sum_i r_i^2$ over the positive and the negative returns | `r number(relative_to_rv5[["rsp5"]], 0.01)` and `r number(relative_to_rv5[["rsn5"]], 0.01)` |
| `rq5` | Realized quarticity $\frac{n}{3} \sum_i r_i^4$ | |

- One-minute returns add noise: `rv1` exceeds `rv5` by `r percent(relative_to_rv5[["rv1"]] - 1)`, most for the stocks with the fewest trades (correlation `r number(noise_trades_correlation, 0.01, style_negative = "minus")` with log trades). Jumps make up about `r percent(1 - relative_to_rv5[["bv5"]])` of the variance (Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard, 2004)

## Volatility has long memory

```{r}
#| label: plot-long-memory
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3.4
# Autocorrelations of log RV up to a year: ES, and the median of the 30
# stocks at each lag
max_lag <- days_per_year
autocorrelations <- volare |>
  reframe(
    lag = seq_len(max_lag),
    autocorrelation = acf(log(rv), lag.max = max_lag, plot = FALSE)$acf[-1],
    .by = symbol
  )
memory <- bind_rows(
  autocorrelations |>
    filter(symbol == "ES") |>
    mutate(series = "ES"),
  autocorrelations |>
    filter(symbol != "ES") |>
    summarize(autocorrelation = median(autocorrelation), .by = lag) |>
    mutate(series = "Dow Jones stocks (median)")
)
es_first <- memory$autocorrelation[memory$series == "ES" & memory$lag == 1]
ar1 <- tibble(lag = seq_len(max_lag), autocorrelation = es_first^lag)
memory_at <- \(series, at) {
  memory$autocorrelation[memory$series == series & memory$lag == at]
}

ggplot(memory, aes(x = lag, y = autocorrelation)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = grey, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(data = ar1, color = grey, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(aes(color = series), linewidth = 0.9) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 26,
    y = -0.08,
    hjust = 0,
    label = "Dashed: an AR(1) with the first autocorrelation of ES",
    color = grey
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("ES" = ku_red, "Dow Jones stocks (median)" = jet)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, days_month, 66, 125, 250)) +
  labs(
    x = "Lag (trading days)",
    y = "Autocorrelation of log RV",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "inside", legend.position.inside = c(0.85, 0.85))
```

- The autocorrelation of log realized variance: `r number(memory_at("ES", 1), 0.01)` at lag 1 and `r number(memory_at("ES", days_month), 0.01)` after a month (`r days_month` trading days) for ES; `r number(memory_at("Dow Jones stocks (median)", 1), 0.01)` and `r number(memory_at("Dow Jones stocks (median)", days_month), 0.01)` for the median Dow Jones stock
- An AR(1) with the same first autocorrelation would be at `r number(es_first^days_month, 0.01)` after a month. Shocks to volatility die out far more slowly than geometrically: **long memory**

## The HAR model

::: {.box}
Corsi (2009): traders with daily, weekly and monthly horizons react to the volatility of their own horizon. Forecast tomorrow's realized variance from today's, the last week's and the last month's
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$
RV_{t+1} = b_0 + b_d\, RV_t + b_w\, RV^{w}_t + b_m\, RV^{m}_t + e_{t+1}
$$

- $RV^{w}_t$ and $RV^{m}_t$: the averages of the last 5 and 22 days' RV, today included. Every past day gets a weight that falls in three steps: a simple approximation of long memory, estimated by OLS
- **log-HAR:** the same regression in $\log RV$. Robust to the few extreme days, and the forecasts stay positive: $\exp\big(\widehat{\log RV}_{t+1} + \hat\sigma_e^2 / 2\big)$, where $\hat\sigma_e^2$ is the residual variance (the mean of a lognormal)
- HARQ (Bollerslev, Patton & Quaedvlieg, 2016) lowers $b_d$ on days when $RV_t$ is imprecise, i.e. when $RQ_t$ is high
:::

## VOLARE in code

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```{r}
#| label: volare-r
# ES: realized variance from 5-minute returns in squared percent, its
# averages over the last week and the last month, and the next day's RV
days_week <- 5
days_month <- 22

har_data <- read_parquet(
  "data/volare_futures_realized_measures_daily.parquet"
) |>
  filter(symbol == "ES") |>
  arrange(date) |>
  transmute(
    date,
    rv = 1e4 * rv5,
    rv_week = slide_dbl(rv, mean, .before = days_week - 1, .complete = TRUE),
    rv_month = slide_dbl(rv, mean, .before = days_month - 1, .complete = TRUE),
    rv_next = lead(rv)
  ) |>
  drop_na()
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: volare-py
#| eval: false
# ES: realized variance from 5-minute returns in squared percent, its
# averages over the last week and the last month, and the next day's RV
days_week = 5
days_month = 22

har_data = (
    pl.read_parquet("data/volare_futures_realized_measures_daily.parquet")
    .filter(pl.col("symbol") == "ES")
    .sort("date")
    .select("date", rv=1e4 * pl.col("rv5"))
    .with_columns(
        rv_week=pl.col("rv").rolling_mean(days_week),
        rv_month=pl.col("rv").rolling_mean(days_month),
        rv_next=pl.col("rv").shift(-1),
    )
    .drop_nulls()
)
```

## HAR in code

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```{r}
#| label: har-r
# Estimate until the end of 2020, then forecast every day
estimation_end <- ymd("2020-12-31")

estimation <- har_data |> filter(date <= estimation_end)
har <- lm(rv_next ~ rv + rv_week + rv_month, data = estimation)
log_har <- lm(
  log(rv_next) ~ log(rv) + log(rv_week) + log(rv_month),
  data = estimation
)

# Next-day forecasts; a log forecast needs the mean of the lognormal
har_forecasts <- har_data |>
  mutate(
    har = predict(har, newdata = har_data),
    log_har = exp(predict(log_har, newdata = har_data) + sigma(log_har)^2 / 2)
  )
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: har-py
#| eval: false
# Estimate until the end of 2020, then forecast every day
estimation_end = date(2020, 12, 31)

estimation = har_data.filter(pl.col("date") <= estimation_end).to_pandas()
har = smf.ols("rv_next ~ rv + rv_week + rv_month", data=estimation).fit()
log_har = smf.ols(
    "np.log(rv_next) ~ np.log(rv) + np.log(rv_week) + np.log(rv_month)",
    data=estimation,
).fit()

# Next-day forecasts; a log forecast needs the mean of the lognormal
har_forecasts = har_data.with_columns(
    har=pl.Series(har.predict(har_data.to_pandas())),
    log_har=pl.Series(
        np.exp(log_har.predict(har_data.to_pandas()) + log_har.scale / 2)
    ),
)
```

## Judging volatility forecasts

::: {.box}
The true variance is never observed. How do we compare forecasts $h_t$ of tomorrow's variance?
:::

::: {.fragment}
- **The proxy:** tomorrow's $RV_{t+1}$, which is far less noisy than $r_{t+1}^2$
- **Losses** that rank forecasts correctly even with a noisy proxy (Patton, 2011):
$$
\text{MSE} = (RV_{t+1} - h_t)^2, \qquad \text{QLIKE} = \frac{RV_{t+1}}{h_t} - \log \frac{RV_{t+1}}{h_t} - 1
$$
- QLIKE depends only on the ratio, so the few extreme days do not dominate it. A forecast that is too low costs more than one that is too high
- **Mincer–Zarnowitz:** in the regression $RV_{t+1} = a + b\, h_t + e_{t+1}$, an unbiased forecast has $a = 0$ and $b = 1$; the $R^2$ measures the fit
- **Out of sample:** estimate until `r year(estimation_end)`, then forecast every day from `r year(estimation_end) + 1` to October 2026 with these coefficients
:::

## HAR against GARCH out of sample

```{r}
#| label: plot-forecast-comparison
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3.4
# Losses relative to HAR for each asset; the median of the 30 stocks
relative_losses <- forecast_losses |>
  mutate(
    QLIKE = qlike / qlike[model == "HAR"],
    MSE = mse / mse[model == "HAR"],
    .by = symbol
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(c(QLIKE, MSE), names_to = "loss", values_to = "relative") |>
  mutate(
    model = factor(model, levels = rev(forecast_models)),
    loss = paste(factor(loss, levels = c("QLIKE", "MSE")), "relative to HAR"),
    loss = fct_inorder(loss)
  )
stock_losses <- relative_losses |> filter(symbol != "ES")
median_losses <- stock_losses |>
  summarize(relative = median(relative), .by = c(model, loss)) |>
  mutate(series = "Dow Jones stocks (median)")
es_losses <- relative_losses |>
  filter(symbol == "ES") |>
  mutate(series = "ES")

ggplot(stock_losses, aes(x = relative, y = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, color = grey, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(color = "#b3b3b3", alpha = 0.6, size = 1.5) +
  geom_point(
    data = bind_rows(median_losses, es_losses),
    aes(color = series),
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~loss, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_color_manual(

  ) +
  labs(x = "Loss relative to HAR (log scale)", y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

beats <- \(winner, loser, measure) {
  forecast_losses |>
    filter(symbol != "ES") |>
    summarize(
      better = .data[[measure]][model == winner] <
        .data[[measure]][model == loser],
      .by = symbol
    ) |>
    pull(better) |>
    sum()
}
es_qlike <- forecast_losses |> filter(symbol == "ES")
```

- Forecasts of the next day's RV from `r year(estimation_end) + 1` to October 2026; grey: each of the 30 Dow Jones stocks; below 1: better than HAR. GARCH forecasts the close-to-close variance and is scaled to the hours of RV; for the stocks, the night carries about `r percent(1 - stocks_garch$garch_scale)` of it
- HAR beats GARCH on QLIKE for `r beats("HAR", "GARCH(1,1)", "qlike")` of 30 stocks and for ES (`r number(es_qlike$qlike[es_qlike$model == "HAR"], 0.001)` against `r number(es_qlike$qlike[es_qlike$model == "GARCH(1,1)"], 0.001)`), on MSE for `r beats("HAR", "GARCH(1,1)", "mse")`. [The log-HAR]{style="white-space: nowrap"} beats HAR on QLIKE for `r beats("log-HAR", "HAR", "qlike")` of 30 stocks
